Termux:X11 embedded native engine and adapted Android JNI integration

Upstream: https://github.com/termux/termux-x11
Exact source: fa3a8b430e2896a19f44c99a9cb056254615ae06
Upstream reference APK version: 1.03.01-fa3a8b4-06.10.26 (not the shipped native binary)
License: GNU GPL version 3; see LICENSE.txt. Native dependencies also retain
 their respective upstream licenses in the source repositories.

This application ships a locally modified, source-built libXlorie.so. It does
not extract its native engine from the upstream nightly APK. The repository's
sources.json retains the upstream reference APK/native checksums, source archive
checksum and exact submodule gitlinks; these are upstream provenance, not hashes
of the modified binary. GitHub-generated source archives omit submodule contents.

scripts/x11_native.py verifies the source archive and every pinned submodule
archive against sources.json and build-inputs.json. Before using a materialized
tree, it compares all files and symlinks against manifests derived directly from
those verified archives; a writable cache marker alone is never trusted.
It applies third_party/termux-x11/overrides/ relative to lorie/src/main/cpp and
builds the Xlorie CMake target, including the rootless tracker and JNI bridge.
The build fingerprint covers override hashes, builder and input pins, and tools.

scripts/x11_assets.py generates artifact-specific sources.json for the APK:
native.modified is true and native.sha256 identifies the actual shipped library.
The upstream reference APK/native records are explicitly nested under
upstream_artifacts. The accompanying native-build.json records the source commit,
override hashes, build fingerprint, toolchain and resulting native checksum.

Retrieve the corresponding upstream source, including build scripts and all
pinned dependencies (do not use submodule update --remote):

  git clone --no-checkout https://github.com/termux/termux-x11.git termux-x11-source
  git -C termux-x11-source checkout --detach fa3a8b430e2896a19f44c99a9cb056254615ae06
  git -C termux-x11-source submodule update --init --recursive

Check the submodule commits against the repository's sources.json. The exact
superproject tree includes CMake recipes, patches and Gradle/toolchain settings.
Native sources are under lorie/src/main/cpp. Apply this project's complete
overrides tree and build with its helper rather than building upstream alone.

From this project's source root:

  python3 scripts/x11_native.py --prepare-only
  python3 scripts/x11_assets.py --native .build/apk/lib/arm64-v8a --assets .build/assets

On Ubuntu aarch64, the helper uses host clang-18 and a locally extracted,
checksum-pinned toolchain: complete official NDK r29 headers and Android API30
link stubs, static C++ runtimes, Termux compiler-rt, and Ubuntu build tools.
X11_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT selects its cache; X11_SOURCE_ROOT selects the pristine source
tree. On other hosts, set ANDROID_NDK_HOME and provide CMake, Ninja, Bison, patch,
and the host C compiler. The standard NDK route also uses Android API30 and
static libc++. No native build failure falls back to the upstream APK library.

The upstream engine's auxiliary TCP knock listener is not disabled by
-nolisten tcp: the embedding service must apply this project's process-wide
network guard before loading/starting it.

This project's adapted Java sources, network guard, packaging scripts and build
configuration are also part of the source needed for the combined application.
Its source distribution must correspond to the specific distributed APK.

A license notice and an upstream link alone are NOT a declaration of GPL
compliance. Before distributing binaries, provide recipients equivalent access
to the complete corresponding source (including every pinned submodule, local
modifications and build/install scripts), applicable notices and any required
installation information under GPLv3. Preserve availability for the required
period; do not rely on the moving nightly tag. The distributor remains
responsible for the combined work's licensing and source-conveyance obligations.

Keyboard data is independently packaged from Ubuntu's xkb-data 2.29-2. Its
source URLs, checksums and copyright/license text are in
third_party/xkeyboard-config/. The compact ZIP contains the complete installed
XKB tree rather than only one keyboard layout.
